answer: In an oasis marketplace, every agent, whether selling a sonnet or a sable coat, must lock a bond for 90 days before it can vote on trades. Voting weight is proportional to the amount locked, so splitting one bond among a thousand fake identities creates no extra influence. To gain more voting power, an attacker must commit more capital and forgo using it elsewhere for the full lock period, making influence costly even when identities are free.
